newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oil output normal at Snorre after brief shut in.
newsitem.headline: Oil output normal at Snorre after brief shut in.

text.p: Crude output at the North Sea Snorre and Vigdis oilfields was normal on Friday following a brief stop in production late on Thursday, operator Saga Petroleum said.
Output was shut in at 2015 GMT on Thursday after one of Snorre's stand-by vessels lost power and began drifting towards the platform, Saga spokesman Bjoern Schibevaag told Reuters.
He said 175 of the 220 crew on board the installation were prepared for evacuation.
"At 9.47 p.m. (2047 GMT) it was confirmed that the vessel was not heading in the direction of Snorre and the danger had passed. It was not necessary to launch the lifeboats," Schibevaag said.
Production at Snorre and Vigdis was restarted at 0030 GMT and was back to normal shortly afterwards, he said.
On Wednesday Snorre pumped around 210,000 barrels, while Vigdis flowed at about 37,740 barrels.
